summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and cardiomyopathy was admitted for recurrent shortness of breath and persistent low-grade fevers. Initial imaging showed right lower lobe consolidation concerning for pneumonia, and she was treated with antibiotics. A thoracentesis was performed for symptomatic pleural effusion, which showed no evidence of infection. Continued fevers prompted further investigation, including a CT-guided lymph node biopsy, which revealed changes consistent with lupus rather than infection or malignancy. Her respiratory symptoms improved with treatment, and she was discharged with a plan for rheumatology follow-up to manage underlying lupus activity as the likely driver of her systemic inflammation.
